text_to_image_prompt: Create a photorealistic fictional adult male head-and-shoulders turnaround on a solid pure white background, landscape approximately 9:4. Three equally sized portraits of one identical person in a horizontal row: left strictly frontal and looking at camera, center exact 90-degree profile facing image-right, right exact 180-degree rear view with no face visible. Complete head and hairstyle visible, upright head, aligned crown and ear heights, matched anatomical scale and neutral eye-level camera, shoulders level. Natural taller oval posterior cranium, rounded crown and full occipital volume, coherent layered hair with natural taper into the upper nape; no flattened skull, bowl-shaped wig or excessive neck exposure. Soft even neutral studio light, realistic skin microtexture, dry detailed hair and matte natural complexion. No oily shine, CGI, beauty filter, text, labels, borders, hands or handheld objects. Character appearance and clothing: Focused athletic confidence. Short black loosely combed hair, hazel eyes. Facial features: broad square jaw, narrow deep-set eyes, wider nose, thin straight lips, slight natural mouth asymmetry. Black zip athletic jacket with subtle white piping.
original_prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
EDIT the attached three-view photographic character sheet. Return a revised version of the SAME sheet, same 1881 x 836 pixels, landscape 9:4, three equal columns. Preserve LEFT frontal portrait and CENTER exact side-profile portrait as closely as possible: same person, facial identity, hairstyle, expression, clothes, accessories, lighting, scale and position.
CRITICAL correction to the RIGHT REAR VIEW ONLY: its hair-covered head currently appears vertically compressed, too short and too wide, like a flattened ball. Reconstruct a naturally proportioned adult back-of-head from the SAME person's front and profile. A real, taller oval cranial vault, rounded crown, full elongated occipital volume, natural taper toward the nape. Maintain matching anatomical scale and camera eye level across all three views. Use the front/profile as anatomical authority; do NOT reproduce the old squashed rear silhouette.
Make a clearly visible correction: the rear hair-covered silhouette must be approximately 18–22% taller and modestly 5–10% narrower than the existing rear silhouette, keeping its top near the same horizontal crown level as the other views. Extend the hair mass DOWNWARD over the occiput and upper nape with believable layered length consistent with the source hairstyle; lower the rear hairline appropriately, avoid a high bowl-cut hairline. Preserve original hair color, curl/wave pattern and styling. Do NOT merely add a fluffy tuft at the top. No huge balloon head, mushroom dome, spherical wig, tiny compressed skull, flat back, overlong exposed neck, new mullet, shoulder-length hair or artificial vertical stretching.
Head remains upright, EXACT 180 degree rear view, face entirely invisible, shoulders level. Ear heights match the front/profile, hair can naturally partially cover ears according to source. Keep rear neck and shoulders consistent with a correctly sized head; re-render this area naturally without distorting clothing. Solid pure white background, same natural matte photorealistic skin and dry detailed hair, neutral soft studio light, no oily shine or CGI. No text, dividers, props or hands. Output the full corrected triptych, not a single rear portrait.
Character 07. Retain this character's short tapered haircut; correct skull proportions and nape coverage without adding a mullet.
